report.summary: Enumerated public symbols and claims in daedalus/providers/_report.py chunk 1 of 1.

handoff.purpose: Shared helpers for building prompts and validating reports for non-agentic providers.

symbols.name: report_instructions
symbols.note: Returns a string instructing the model to output a JSON object with specific keys.

symbols.name: build_prompt
symbols.note: Returns (system, user) messages for a read-only, non-agentic provider.

symbols.name: extract_json
symbols.note: Parses JSON from text, attempting to find JSON if initial parse fails.

symbols.name: coerce_report
symbols.note: Fills missing keys with defaults and validates report via validate_report.

symbols.name: blocked_report
symbols.note: Returns a blocked report dict with given summary and todo.

symbols.name: budget_refusal_report
symbols.note: Returns a blocked report for a BudgetError, including budget detail.

symbols.name: reserve_or_report

claims.text: DeepSeek json_object mode requires the literal word "json" AND an example of the desired shape in the prompt; both are present here.
claims.why: The comment claims DeepSeek json_object mode requirements; this chunk does not contain any DeepSeek-specific code or configuration to verify that claim.

claims.text: Total inlined-context budget for non-agentic providers (chars). Keeps prompts small per the token-efficiency rules; sensitive files are excluded upstream.
claims.why: The constant is defined as 24_000, but the claim about 'sensitive files are excluded upstream' cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: A billable provider must reserve BEFORE it calls out, and must turn a refusal into a valid agent_report_v1 rather than an exception
claims.why: The claim refers to behavior outside this chunk (agent_report_v1, reservation before call) which is not present in this code.

claims.text: The two helpers below are the whole integration surface; see daedalus/budget.py for why enforcement cannot live in one place.
claims.why: The claim references daedalus/budget.py which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: FAIL CLOSED: every BudgetError -- refused ceiling, unreadable ledger, unobtainable lock, unpriceable vendor -- lands in the second branch. There is no path through this function that returns (None, None) and lets the caller carry on.
claims.why: The function catches BudgetError and returns (None, envelope) in that case; if no exception, it returns (res, None). Since it always returns either (res, None) or (None, envelope), and never (None, None), the claim holds for this code.

claims.text: The blocked report for a refused call. NAMES the numbers.
claims.why: The function creates a blocked_report with budget detail including numbers from exc.as_dict() or str(exc), thus naming the numbers.

claims.text: A refusal the operator cannot read is a refusal the operator switches off, so the ceiling, the spend and the refused label all survive into the report body and into handoff in machine-readable form.
claims.why: The function includes budget detail in handoff via blocked_report, and the summary includes the exception string. The claim about machine-readable form is supported by exc.as_dict() for BudgetRefused.

claims.text: (reservation, None) when the call may proceed, (None, envelope) when it may not.
claims.why: The function returns res, None on success and None, envelope on BudgetError, as implemented.

claims.text: Return ONLY a json object with exactly these keys: status (done|blocked|needs_review|failed), summary (<=...), files_changed (array), tests_run (array), risks (array), todos (array), handoff (object). You are READ-ONLY: you cannot edit files or run tests, so files_changed and tests_run must be []. Put any proposed edit as text inside handoff.
claims.why: The function returns a string containing exactly that instruction, including the specified keys and constraints.
The function includes that exact example in its return string.

claims.text: Fill any missing report keys with safe defaults, then validate.
claims.why: The function supplies defaults for missing keys and calls validate_report.

observations.what: The constant MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS (24000) is defined but never used in this chunk.
build_prompt does not enforce MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS on context_text; it passes it as-is.
extract_json raises raw json.JSONDecodeError or ValueError without wrapping in a custom exception; callers may need to handle generic exceptions.
